findings.message: kapāla-mālikā-dhara is typed 'upapada', and the note says dhara is formed with the affix ac and 'only stands at the end of a compound'. An upapada compound (rule 2.2.19) needs a kṛt affix that a grammar rule attaches only when a specific preceding word is present. The general agent affix ac (the pacādi set, rule 3.1.134) has no such condition. mw-dhara.md also lists dhara as a standalone word: 'mf(ā)n. (√dhṛ) bearing, supporting (scil. the world, said of Kṛṣṇa and Śiva), MBh.' The usual analysis is therefore a tatpuruṣa with the genitive, 'kapālamālikāyāḥ dharaḥ'. The meaning does not change, so I am flagging this rather than failing it.
findings.suggested_fix: Set type 'tatpuruṣa', subtype 'ṣaṣṭhī', vigraha 'कपालानां मालिका कपालमालिका, तस्याः धरः, तम्'. Remove 'only stands at the end of a compound' from c5.note (en/hi), or record upapada as an alternative analysis.
